Title: Current reference setup
Claim: Current headset is Creative Sound BlasterX H7 Tournament Edition; current PC path is 3.5mm analog into Sound BlasterX AE-5 headphone output; wired/wireless is not a purchase priority.

Title: Current listening preference
Claim: User has reported that AE-5 Direct Mode sounds cleaner than virtualized/effect processing; competitive FPS is low priority.
Notes: Subjective user preference; not a product measurement.

Title: Sound BlasterX H7 Tournament Edition specifications
Claim: H7 Tournament Edition uses 50mm neodymium drivers, 20Hz-20kHz response, 32 ohm impedance, 118dB/mW sensitivity and supports USB plus 3.5mm analog connection.
Notes: Official launch specifications; official 364g figure includes mic and cables.

Title: Sound BlasterX AE-5 technical specifications
Claim: AE-5 uses ESS ES9016K2M DAC and Xamp headphone amplifier with 1 ohm output impedance, 16-600 ohm supported headphone range, 232mW at 16 ohm and 46.8mW at 600 ohm.
Notes: H7 32 ohm load is comfortably within supported range.

Title: Sound Blaster Command Software Guide
Claim: Direct Mode outputs audio in original form and disables applied audio effects until Direct Mode is disabled.
Notes: Relevant to separating AE-5 Direct Mode from SBX-processed listening.

Title: Sound BlasterX H7 Tournament measurements
Claim: Passive analog measurement shows elevated bass around 80-300Hz, strongly recessed presence/mids versus bass, decent but somewhat coarse treble, low-frequency distortion generally below 1%, and an impedance response that changes little with amplifier output impedance.
Notes: Single independent measurement rig; very relevant because current H7 USB DSP is bypassed by analog AE-5 connection.

Title: Creative Sound BlasterX H7 Tournament Edition review
Claim: Review reports high comfort, wide sound separation, strong gaming/movie performance, less prominent mids and somewhat emphasized highs; pop/EDM fare better than some organic genres.
Notes: Listening review includes Creative processing context, so it is not treated as a pure passive analog measurement.

Title: Sound BlasterX H7 Tournament Edition review
Claim: Review reports comfortable long sessions, crisp/accurate sound, and good 3.5mm positional performance; it also notes connection-mode differences.
Notes: Useful subjective cross-check; not a controlled measurement.

Title: Seven-year H7 Tournament Edition ownership report
Claim: A long-term owner reports seven years of use before leather-effect material flaking became a replacement reason.
Notes: Single anecdote; useful as long-term material-aging evidence only.

Title: H7 Tournament Edition comfort recommendation
Claim: A user recommendation describes the H7 Tournament Edition as well built and comfortable for long play periods.
Notes: Single community anecdote; corroborates professional comfort reviews.
